name: fix_kotlin_insecure_random_token
description: java.util.Random for session tokens (predictable LCG seeded from clock time) -> java.security.SecureRandom; incomplete-fix broken uses SecureRandom but with a hardcoded seed, making it deterministic again
prompts: TokenGenerator.generate() in TokenGenerator.kt uses java.util.Random to produce session tokens. java.util.Random is a linear-congruential PRNG seeded from the clock by default - not cryptographically secure, and an attacker who narrows down the seed (often just the millisecond the process started) can predict every token it will ever produce. Replace it with java.security.SecureRandom, constructed with NO explicit seed (let the platform seed it from a real entropy source) - a hardcoded or fixed seed is just as predictable as the original bug, even with SecureRandom. Keep generate()'s signature and output shape (32 lowercase hex characters from 16 random bytes).
